headline: COPPER DROPS 0.64% TO $13,398/T AS IRAN FLARE-UP REIGNITES RATE FEARS — BASE METALS TAKE BIGGEST HIT IN TWO WEEKS
snippet: LME three-month copper slipped 0.64% to $13,398.5/t on July 13 as renewed US-Iran hostilities — including Iran's re-closure of the Strait of Hormuz — drove crude higher and reignited rate-hike inflation fears that suppress manufacturing demand expectations. The energy-driven inflation spike, arriving a day before the June CPI print, stoked fears that elevated central bank rates would persist; copper's pullback from the $13,700 range is the sharpest two-week correction since the initial Hormuz closure in early July, with the dollar's strength amplifying pressure across the base metals complex alongside the risk-off bid.

headline: JUNE CPI BINARY: ANALYSTS SEE FIRST NEGATIVE MOM HEADLINE IN 18 MONTHS — WHAT IT MEANS FOR GOLD ON JULY 14
snippet: TradingKey's pre-CPI analysis maps the binary for markets heading into Tuesday's June inflation report: economists project a -0.1% month-over-month headline reading — the first negative print in 18 months, driven by June energy disinflation before the July Iran war spike — which would pull the year-over-year rate toward 3.4–3.8% from May's 4.2% reading and collapse September rate-hike odds currently above 60%; a 4.0%+ YoY print replicating May's pace would validate Fed hawkishness and extend gold's consolidation below $4,150. May 2026 CPI at 4.2% was the fastest since early 2023, making Tuesday the most consequential macro event since the April FOMC meeting.

headline: ISS BACKS $18.5B EQUINOX-ORLA ALL-SHARE DEAL — LARGEST NORTH AMERICAN GOLD MERGER VOTE SET FOR JULY 22
snippet: ISS recommended July 10 that Equinox Gold shareholders vote FOR the all-share acquisition of Orla Mining at the July 22 special meeting, describing the deal as 'strategically sound' and noting it 'diversifies the asset base and enhances long-term production potential.' The combined company would carry an approximate US$18.5 billion market value, projected 2026 production exceeding one million ounces, and assets spanning Mexico, the US, Brazil, and Suriname — both boards are unanimous FOR, the proxy voting deadline is July 20 at 9 a.m. Vancouver time, and regulatory clearances have already been secured under the Investment Canada Act.

headline: SILVERCO FIRES 2 RIGS AT MEXICO LA NEGRA SILVER PROJECT — 15,000M PROGRAM TARGETS HIGH-GRADE FEED FOR MINE PLAN (TSXV:SICO)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Silverco Mining Ltd.
snippet: Silverco Mining Ltd. (TSXV: SICO) announced July 13 the mobilization of two exploration drill rigs at its 100%-owned La Negra Project in Querétaro, Mexico, beginning a planned 15,000-metre 2026 program focused on testing high-grade silver zones with potential to feed directly into the mine plan early in mine life. La Negra runs alongside an ongoing 30,000-metre program at the Cusi silver mine — where previous drilling returned up to 1,100 g/t Ag over 10.3 metres — with Cusi's restart targeted for late Q4 2026; an updated La Negra mineral resource estimate and life-of-mine plan are expected in H2 2026, making Silverco one of the most active multi-asset silver developers in Mexico.

headline: LITHIUM CARBONATE HITS 3-MONTH LOW AT CNY 154,000 AS CATL, BALD HILL, AND FINNISS MINE RESTARTS CONVERGE
snippet: Lithium carbonate prices have retreated to CNY 154,000/t — the lowest in three months — as three major global mine restarts converge on supply simultaneously: CATL's Jianxiawo mine in Yichun (46,000 t/yr LCE capacity, roughly 3% of 2025 global output) cleared its safety production permit, Mineral Resources' Bald Hill mine in Western Australia is delivering first spodumene concentrate in July following an 18-month suspension, and Core Lithium's Finniss project in the Northern Territory is ramping back toward 214,000 tpa capacity. The market panic over tight supply that drove lithium above CNY 190,000 earlier in 2026 has dissipated — though EV battery and AI-driven energy storage demand continues to provide a structural floor independent of near-term supply pressure.

headline: 'GOLD WINS EITHER WAY': THE TWO-SCENARIO CASE FOR $4,000+ METAL REGARDLESS OF TUESDAY'S CPI OUTCOME
snippet: Advantage Gold's pre-CPI analysis argues that gold is structurally positioned to win under either June outcome: a hot print validates the inflation-hedge narrative and increases institutional allocation, while a cool or negative print accelerates rate-cut expectations — and every major Fed easing cycle since 2001 has been accompanied by gold outperformance. Underpinning both scenarios: central banks globally purchased 244 tonnes of gold in Q1 2026, up 17% quarter-over-quarter, with 45% of surveyed central banks planning to increase reserves in the next 12 months — a structural demand floor that operates regardless of which direction the Fed ultimately moves.

headline: RUSH RARE METALS FILES SHAREHOLDER CIRCULAR FOR MYRIAD URANIUM MERGER — FIRST CSE URANIUM-RARE EARTH COMBINATION PLAY (CSE:RSH)
snippet: Rush Rare Metals Corp. (CSE: RSH) filed its management information circular on July 13 for the special shareholder meeting to approve its all-share merger with Myriad Uranium Corp. (CSE: M), under which Myriad will acquire all Rush shares at a ratio of 0.5405 Myriad shares per Rush share. The combination diversifies Myriad's uranium-focused portfolio with Rush's rare earth and critical minerals assets — creating one of the few CSE-listed companies with combined exposure to both nuclear fuel and rare earth supply chains at a time when Western governments are funding both sectors simultaneously.

headline: COT JULY 10: GOLD SPECS NEAR 7-MONTH LOW AT 194,000 COMEX CONTRACTS — WASHOUT POSITIONING SIGNALS CONTRARIAN RALLY SETUP
snippet: The July 10 Commitments of Traders report shows COMEX gold speculative net-long positioning at approximately 194,000 contracts — down 13% from January 2026's crowded peak — indicating that systematic trend-followers have already materially reduced gold exposure through the summer correction. Historically, gold has generated its strongest 3-to-6-month forward returns when speculative positioning is this compressed relative to cyclical peaks; the COT washout setup, combined with gold's mid-July seasonal inflection window and the CPI binary arriving July 14, represents the technical backdrop that has preceded the most explosive autumn gold rallies in the current bull market cycle.

headline: ALL 18 RARE EARTH ELEMENTS RALLY IN JULY — GERMANIUM +27.8%, DYSPROSIUM +25.4%; CHINA'S EXPORT CONTROLS DRIVE HISTORIC BREADTH
snippet: The July 2026 Rare Earth Market Outlook documents a rare breadth reading: all 18 tracked elements rose in price during July with zero declines — led by germanium's 27.8% domestic surge driven by China's semiconductor-critical element export controls and dysprosium's 25.4% gain as permanent magnet demand from wind turbines and EV motors outstrips ex-China separation capacity. The structural momentum index has reached its 2026 high, yet the REEx tracker warns that Chinese leverage has actually increased through tighter export controls, and Japanese manufacturers are flagging heavy REE shortages with no adequate non-Chinese supply to replace restricted dysprosium and terbium volumes.

headline: GOLD MINERS NEAR-RECORD Q2: PROFITS TRACKING 50% HIGHER YOY WITH 12 STRAIGHT QUARTERS OF EARNINGS GROWTH — STOCKS MOST OVERSOLD SINCE LAST BULL WAS BORN
snippet: Adam Hamilton's Q2 2026 gold mining analysis documents a structural earnings-to-price disconnect: gold miners are tracking their 12th consecutive quarter of substantial earnings growth, with Q2'26 profits running approximately 50% higher year-over-year against an average AISC of $1,703/oz — yet gold mining equities are at their most oversold relative to fundamentals since the nascent phase of the current bull market. Hamilton's thesis: near-record Q2 results combined with the most compressed gold-equity-to-metal-price ratio of the current cycle represent a historically rare alignment of cheap valuations and strong earnings momentum, with the seasonal mid-July inflection providing the timing catalyst.
